worked.title: Q1 · Triangular matrix: eigenvalues, eigenspace, independence (7 marks)

problem.text: A = [[−2, 0, 0, 0], [−1, 3, 0, 0], [0, 1, −1, 0], [−1, −1, 0, 5]]. (a) All eigenvalues; the eigenspace V of the largest; a basis and dimension of V. [1 + 2 + 2] (b) Are the columns of A independent? [2M]

steps.label: (a) Eigenvalues
steps.text: Lower triangular ⇒ eigenvalues are the diagonal: **−2, 3, −1, 5** [1M].

steps.label: (a) λ = 5
steps.text: (A − 5I)X = 0: −7x₁ = 0, −x₁ − 2x₂ = 0, x₂ − 6x₃ = 0, −x₁ − x₂ = 0 ⇒ x₁ = x₂ = x₃ = 0, x₄ free [1M].

steps.label: (b)
steps.text: Σaᵢvᵢ = 0 gives −2a₁ = 0, −a₁ + 3a₂ = 0, a₂ − a₃ = 0, −a₁ − a₂ + 5a₄ = 0 [1M] ⇒ all aᵢ = 0 ⇒ **independent** [1M]. (Quicker: det A = (−2)(3)(−1)(5) = 30 ≠ 0, full marks.)

worked.answer: Eigenvalues −2, 3, −1, 5; V = span{(0, 0, 0, 1)}, dim 1; columns independent (det 30).
worked.priorityWhy: Recent paper: sit it as a timed mock (≈ 3.4 min per mark)

worked.title: Q2 · Positive definite, inner product, Gram–Schmidt (8 marks)

problem.text: A = [[3, 1, 0], [1, 1, 0], [0, 0, 2]]. (a) Prove A is symmetric positive definite. [2M] (b) Define an inner product with it. [1M] (c) Show (1, 2, −1) and (2, −1, 0) are not orthogonal under it. [2M] (d) Gram–Schmidt on v₁ = (1, 2, −1), v₂ = (2, −1, 0) under it. [3M]

steps.label: (a)
steps.text: A = Aᵀ [0.5M]. Leading minors 3, 3 − 1 = 2 [0.5M], 2 × 2 = 4, all > 0 ⇒ PD [1M].

steps.label: (b)
steps.text: ⟨X, Y⟩ = XᵀAY [0.5M] = x₁(3y₁ + y₂) + x₂(y₁ + y₂) + 2x₃y₃ [0.5M].

worked.priorityWhy: Recent paper: sit it as a timed mock (≈ 3.4 min per mark)

worked.title: Q3 · Line search by binary search, then the exact optimum (7 marks)

problem.text: L(w₁, w₂) = w₁⁴ + w₂⁴ − (w₁ + w₂), start (0, 0), φ(α) = L((0, 0) + αd) with d = −∇L(0, 0). (a) Binary search on [0, 2]: the interval after two iterations. [4M] (b) Minimise φ with the second-derivative test; is the interval shrinking towards it? [3M]

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: This paper's symbol is kept: the learning rate is **α** (η on the lecture boards), and φ(α) = L((0, 0) + αd).

steps.label: (b)
steps.text: φ′ = 0 ⇒ α = (1/4)^(1/3) ≈ **0.63** [1M]; φ″ = 24α² > 0 ⇒ minimum [1.5M]; 0.63 ∈ [0.5, 1], so the interval is closing in on it [0.5M].

worked.answer: Intervals [0, 1] then [0.5, 1]; exact optimum α ≈ 0.63, inside the final interval.
worked.priorityWhy: Recent paper: sit it as a timed mock (≈ 3.4 min per mark)

worked.title: Q4 · GD with momentum, two iterations (4 marks)

problem.text: Consider the function J(w₀, w₁) = (w₀ − 3)² + (w₁ − 3)². We wish to minimise J(w₀, w₁) using the Gradient Descent algorithm with momentum. The initial parameter values are (w₀⁰, w₁⁰) = (2, 2), the learning rate is η = 0.05, the momentum parameter is β = 0.5, and the initial velocity vector is (v₀⁰, v₁⁰) = (0, 0). Compute the parameter value (w₀¹, w₁¹) after the first iteration and (w₀², w₁²) after the second iteration. [4M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Whether you can run the momentum recursion forward for two iterations without a sign slip. The answer key gives 1 mark each for v¹, w¹, v² and w².

steps.label: Plan of attack
steps.text: 1. Write the update rule. 2. Find the gradient formula once. 3. For each iteration, in this order: **gradient at the current point → new velocity → new position**. 4. Box w¹ and w².

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: The paper's symbols are the board's: η step size, β momentum, v velocity. Superscripts count iterations: w⁰ = start, w¹ after iteration 1, w² after iteration 2.

steps.label: STEP 1 · Update rule
steps.text: vᵗ⁺¹ = βvᵗ − η∇J(wᵗ)  and  wᵗ⁺¹ = wᵗ + vᵗ⁺¹, with v⁰ = (0, 0).

steps.label: STEP 2 · Gradient formula
steps.text: ∂J/∂w₀ = 2(w₀ − 3) × 1 = 2(w₀ − 3) (chain rule on (w₀ − 3)²); ∂J/∂w₁ = 2(w₁ − 3). So ∇J(w₀, w₁) = (2(w₀ − 3), 2(w₁ − 3)). The minimum is at (3, 3), where ∇J = (0, 0).

steps.label: STEP 3 · Iteration 1: gradient at w⁰
steps.text: ∇J(2, 2) = (2(2 − 3), 2(2 − 3)) = (2 × (−1), 2 × (−1)) = **(−2, −2)**. Negative slope ⇒ J decreases as w increases, so the step will be positive.

steps.label: STEP 10 · Sense check
steps.text: Plain GD would give w² = 2.1 − 0.05 × (−1.8) = 2.19. Momentum reached 2.24: the extra 0.05 is β × v¹. Both coordinates are identical because J is symmetric in w₀ and w₁ and the start is symmetric, so you could compute one coordinate and copy it.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Using ∇J at the new point instead of the point you are leaving (the gradient for v² is at w¹, not w²).
• Sign slips: −η × (−2) is **+0.1**.
• Adding β to the position instead of the velocity, or forgetting βv¹ in iteration 2.
• Writing only w¹ and w² without v¹, v²: two of the four marks are for the velocities.

worked.title: Q6 · Soft-margin SVM: hinge form and objective (7 marks)

problem.text: X1 (3, 3) +1, X2 (5, 5) +1, X3 (3, 0) −1, X4 (5, 0) −1. (a) Soft-margin primal. [1M] (b) Show the hinge (unconstrained) form. [2M] (c) For w = (1, −1), b = 0: each yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) [2M], each hinge loss [1M], total objective with C = 1 [1M].

steps.label: (a)
steps.text: min ½(w₁² + w₂²) + C(ξ₁ + … + ξ₄) s.t. yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) ≥ 1 − ξᵢ written out for all four points, ξᵢ ≥ 0.

steps.label: (b)
steps.text: ξᵢ ≥ 1 − yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) and ξᵢ ≥ 0, and the objective pushes ξᵢ down, so ξᵢ = max(0, 1 − yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b)) [1M + 1M].
